summary: A korban that was shechted with a different korban in mind is still kosher, but it does not count for the owner. A korban Pesach and a chatas become pasul this way, and Rabbi Eliezer says an asham does too.

chunks.en: All korbanos that were shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: All slaughtered offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake,
chunks.stMore: i.e., during the slaughtering the slaughterer’s intent was to sacrifice a different offering,

words.note: Shechted while thinking of a different kind of korban.

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה.
chunks.en: are kosher, but they do not count for the owner's duty.
chunks.st: are fit, and one may continue their sacrificial rites and partake of their meat where that applies. But these offerings did not satisfy the obligation of the owner, who is therefore required to bring another offering.

chunks.en: Except for the korban Pesach and the chatas.
chunks.st: This is the halakha with regard to all offerings except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering.
chunks.stMore: In those cases, if the owner sacrificed them not for their own sake, they are unfit. But there is a difference between the two exceptions.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach is pasul only at its own time,
chunks.st: The Paschal offering is unfit only when sacrificed not for its sake at its appointed time, on the fourteenth day of Nisan after noon,

words.note: The fourteenth of Nisan, after midday.

chunks.en: and the chatas at any time.
chunks.st: while the sin offering is unfit any time that it is sacrificed not for its sake.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: also the asham.
chunks.st: The guilt offering too
chunks.stMore: is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake. According to his opinion, the correct reading of the mishna is:

words.note: A korban brought to fix certain sins.

chunks.en: So the korban Pesach is pasul at its own time,
chunks.st: The Paschal offering is unfit only at its appointed time,

chunks.en: and the chatas and the asham
chunks.st: while the sin offering and the guilt offering

chunks.en: at any time.
chunks.st: are unfit at all times.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said in explanation:

chunks.en: The chatas comes for a sin,
chunks.st: The sin offering is brought for performance of a transgression

chunks.en: and the asham comes for a sin.
chunks.st: and the guilt offering is brought for performance of a transgression.

chunks.en: Just as a chatas is pasul when it is not for its own sake,
chunks.st: Just as a sin offering is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake,

chunks.en: so too an asham is pasul when it is not for its own sake.
chunks.st: so too, the guilt offering is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake.

summary: Some Rabbis add more rules about a korban shechted for the wrong purpose. Shimon, brother of Azarya, says: if it was shechted for a holier korban it is kosher, but for a less holy korban it is pasul.

chunks.en: Yosei ben Choni says,
chunks.st: Yosei ben Ḥoni says:
chunks.stMore: Not only are the Paschal offering and the sin offering unfit when slaughtered not for their sake,

chunks.en: korbanos shechted for the sake of a Pesach or a chatas
chunks.st: but also other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a sin offering

chunks.en: are pasul. Shimon, the brother of Azarya, says:
chunks.st: are unfit. Shimon, brother of Azarya, says that this is the distinction: With regard to all offerings,

chunks.en: If he shechted them for a korban holier than they are,
chunks.st: if one slaughtered them for the sake of an offering whose level of sanctity is greater than theirs,

chunks.en: they are kosher. For a korban less holy than they are,
chunks.st: they are fit; if one slaughtered them for the sake of an offering whose level of sanctity is less than theirs,

chunks.en: they are pasul. How so?
chunks.st: they are unfit. How so?

chunks.he: קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
chunks.en: The holiest korbanos, shechted for the sake of less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: Offerings of the most sacred order, e.g., sin offerings and burnt offerings, that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity, e.g., peace offerings,

words.note: Like the olah and the chatas.

chunks.he: פְּסוּלִין. קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים,
chunks.en: are pasul. Less holy korbanos shechted for the holiest korbanos
chunks.st: are unfit. Offerings of lesser sanctity that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of the most sacred order

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרִין. הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים,
chunks.en: are kosher. A bechor or maaser shechted for a shelamim
chunks.st: are fit. Likewise, there is a distinction between different offerings of lesser sanctity. The firstborn animal and the animal tithe that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering

words.note: A firstborn animal, given to the Kohen.
Every tenth animal, set aside as holy.
A korban that the owner shares in eating.

chunks.en: are kosher. But a shelamim shechted for a bechor
chunks.st: are fit, as the sanctity of peace offerings is greater. Peace offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn

chunks.en: or for maaser is pasul.
chunks.st: animal or for the sake of an animal tithe are unfit.

summary: A korban Pesach shechted for the wrong purpose on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan: Rabbi Yehoshua says it is kosher and Ben Beseira says it is pasul. Ben Azzai shares a tradition from seventy-two elders.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that he shechted on the morning of the fourteenth
chunks.st: With regard to the Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth
chunks.stMore: of Nisan, the day when the Paschal offering should be slaughtered in the afternoon,

chunks.en: not for its own sake,
chunks.st: if he did so not for its sake,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says it is kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit

chunks.en: as if it was shechted on the thirteenth.
chunks.st: as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth
chunks.stMore: of Nisan. An animal consecrated as a Paschal offering that was slaughtered not at its designated time for the sake of a different offering is fit for sacrifice as a peace offering.

chunks.en: Ben Beseira says it is pasul,
chunks.st: Ben Beteira deems it unfit

chunks.en: as if it was shechted in the afternoon.
chunks.st: as though it were slaughtered in the afternoon of the fourteenth.

words.note: The afternoon, the right time for shechting the korban Pesach.

chunks.st: Shimon ben Azzai said:

chunks.en: are kosher, but they do not count for the owner's duty,

chunks.st: except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering. Based on that version,

chunks.en: Ben Azzai added only the olah,

summary: A korban Pesach or chatas becomes pasul if any of its four main jobs is done with the wrong purpose in mind. Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eliezer argue about carrying the blood to the mizbeach.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach or chatas that he shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: With regard to the Paschal offering and the sin offering, where one slaughtered them not for their sake,

chunks.en: or he caught the blood, or carried it,
chunks.st: or where he collected their blood in a vessel, conveyed this blood to the altar,

chunks.en: or threw it, for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: or sprinkled this blood on the altar not for their sake,

chunks.en: or for their sake and then not for their sake,
chunks.st: or where he performed one of these sacrificial rites for their sake and not for their sake,

chunks.en: or not for their sake and then for their sake,
chunks.st: or not for their sake and for their sake,

chunks.en: they are pasul. What is for their sake and not for their sake?
chunks.st: in all these cases the offerings are unfit. How are these rites performed for their sake and not for their sake?

chunks.en: For the sake of a Pesach and for the sake of a shelamim.
chunks.st: In a case where one slaughtered the Paschal offering for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering.

chunks.en: And not for their sake and then for their sake?
chunks.st: How are these rites performed not for their sake and for their sake?

chunks.en: For the sake of a shelamim and for the sake of a Pesach.
chunks.st: In a case where one slaughtered the Paschal offering for the sake of a peace offering and for the sake of a Paschal offering.

chunks.en: Because a korban can become pasul in four jobs:
chunks.st: The offering is unfit because a slaughtered offering is disqualified due to prohibited intent in four matters:

chunks.en: shechting, catching the blood, carrying it, and throwing it.
chunks.st: In the performance of the sacrificial rites of slaughtering the animal, in collecting the blood, in conveying the blood, and in sprinkling the blood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says it stays kosher if it happened while carrying,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems the offering fit if the prohibited intent was during the rite of conveying the blood,

chunks.en: because Rabbi Shimon used to say,
chunks.st: as he would say:

chunks.en: It is impossible without shechting,
chunks.st: It is impossible to sacrifice an offering without slaughtering the animal,

chunks.en: or without catching the blood or throwing it,
chunks.st: or without collection of the blood, or without sprinkling the blood,

chunks.en: but it is possible without carrying it.
chunks.st: but it is possible to sacrifice an offering without conveying the blood to the altar. How so?

chunks.en: He can shecht next to the mizbeach and throw.
chunks.st: If one slaughters the animal alongside the altar and sprinkles
chunks.stMore: the blood, the blood does not need to be conveyed. Therefore, the rite of conveying the blood is not significant enough to cause the offering to be disqualified due to prohibited intent while performing it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: If he carries where he needs to carry it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who conveys the blood in a situation where he is required to convey it,

chunks.en: the wrong thought makes it pasul.
chunks.st: prohibited intent while conveying it disqualifies the offering.

chunks.en: But where he does not need to carry it,
chunks.st: If he conveys the blood in a situation where he is not required to convey it,

chunks.en: the wrong thought does not make it pasul.
chunks.st: prohibited intent while conveying it does not disqualify the offering.
